intro: Lesson 87: Revision: movement of substances and transport in plants and humans. Answer every question. Show your working. Mark it with the mark scheme and log any errors in your repair list.

questions.q: A 3 cm cube has SA:V of...
questions.a: B) 2:1. SA = 54 cm², V = 27 cm³, ratio 2:1.

questions.q: Which process needs energy from respiration?
Which vessel carries blood away from the heart?
Large organisms need transport systems because their SA:V is...
Big question: why does a whale need a heart but an amoeba does not?
questions.a: The whale's small SA:V and long distances mean diffusion alone is too slow, so it needs a pumped transport system.

questions.q: Describe the role of the xylem and phloem.
questions.a: Xylem carries water and mineral ions from roots to the rest of the plant (1); phloem carries sucrose and amino acids between leaves and other parts (1).
questions.model: Two tissues, one mark each. Xylem: what (water and mineral ions) and where (from roots upwards). Phloem: what (sucrose and amino acids) and where (leaves to other parts).

questions.q: Explain why arteries have thick, elastic walls.
questions.a: Blood leaves the heart at high pressure (1); thick elastic walls withstand and even out the pressure (1).

questions.q: Describe the path of blood from the vena cava to the aorta, naming chambers, valves and vessels. Portal response box.
questions.a: Vena cava, right atrium (1), valve, right ventricle (1), pulmonary artery to lungs (1), pulmonary vein (1), left atrium, valve, left ventricle (1), aorta (1).
questions.model: Teacher writes the first two marking points: 'Deoxygenated blood enters the right atrium from the vena cava, then passes through a valve into the right ventricle.'

questions.q: Potato cylinders: in water +10%, in 0.5 M sucrose -8%. Explain both results.
questions.a: Water: higher water concentration outside (1), water enters by osmosis (1); 0.5 M: lower water concentration outside (1), water leaves by osmosis (1).

questions.q: Explain how heart rate changes during exercise and why.
questions.a: Heart rate increases (1); muscles respire faster and need more oxygen and glucose (1) and CO₂ must be removed faster (1). Adrenaline also raises heart rate.
